source.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Atmospheric Rivers in GraphCast
source.authors: Madelyn Mathai; Timothy B. Higgins; K. Grise; Chirag Agarwal; Antonios Mamalakis

page_placements.theme: Nested-prefix (Matryoshka-type) objectives order latents by granularity

record.tranche_reason: The study measures parent–child nesting and absorption-like behavior in a Matryoshka SAE, but concludes that the observed relationship is part–whole nesting rather than feature splitting. In its examined pair, the parent does not cede the child’s high-IVT cases.
record.gate_note: The study does not vary dictionary size. Its comparison of Standard and Matryoshka SAEs across model depths, and its causal interventions on AR concepts, do not test increasing-size feature splitting. Rows below cover its direct measurements of nested features and whether the parent stops firing where the child fires. The reported causal effects on precipitation and other atmospheric quantities are not rows because they do not measure the claim’s splitting or absorption behavior.
record.test_reason: New setting (a GraphCast GNN weather model, Matryoshka SAE at fixed width 4,096). It measures parent–child nesting by spatial containment and checks whether the parent cedes the child's cases, which is absorption. Only one pair is characterized, and there is no dictionary-size sweep. The authors argue the nesting is part–whole, not feature splitting. That is a framing argument, not a separate result, so T3 fits better than T5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors' main conclusion is that GraphCast computes AR intensity (IVT) as a stable, causal internal variable. The Matryoshka SAE addresses it stably and exposes nesting, in which child 3153 nests by intensity within parent 99 without absorption. The child detects ARs but does not drive them, whereas concept 99 is causal via a moisture channel.
record.recipe_differences: Uses standard and Matryoshka SAEs trained on GraphCast activations at fixed dictionary width 4,096, and measures spatial containment among Matryoshka prefix groups. It does not compare increasing dictionary sizes.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports different SAE architectures and depths, but does not report that these settings change the measured parent–child containment result.

fits_no_version.finding: Nested pairs found in the Matryoshka sweep are asymmetric: the child covers only a few percent of the parent's footprint. The authors call this a part–whole relation rather than feature splitting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-level nesting between Matryoshka prefix groups reflects part–whole refinement, distinct from splitting into copies of the same concept.

record.peer_reviewed: Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning: workshop at NeurIPS 2026
record.problems: Only one parent–child pair is characterized in the main analysis. The study does not test decoder-direction proximity, a range of dictionary sizes, or whether changes to size or sparsity alter absorption.
record.rows_left_out: Causal steering results in Section 3.2 and Figure 3 were left out because they measure changes in AR intensity and precipitation, not feature splitting or parent–child absorption. Figure 4 compares SAE architectures and depths at fixed width, not dictionary sizes.

untested.parts: There is no dictionary-size sweep. Width is fixed at 4,096, and the study does not examine whether finer features replace a coarse one.
There are no large language models and no open SAE releases, and there is no size-related splitting test.
Decoder-direction proximity is not measured. Only one pair is characterized beyond aggregate sweep counts.
Absorption is not measured in the Standard SAE. The study does not vary SAE size or sparsity, and has no systematic absorption metric beyond one pair.
The study does not test whether larger latents decompose into smaller ones, or whether novel latents appear across sizes.
There is no Standard-vs-Matryoshka comparison of splitting or absorption, and no test of whether splitting is an artifact of the objective.

missing.what: Asymmetry of nested pairs: the child covers only a few percent of the parent's own footprint. This is stated qualitatively, with no exact number.

record.verdict_notes: r1 bears on two versions with different states (V3 observed, V4 absent), which one state field cannot hold. The study cites A is for Absorption, which is an original source, but the study itself is not one, so verdicts are allowed. Steering results and the depth comparison were correctly left out.

versions.untested_parts: No SAE dictionary-size sweep or comparison of coarse and finer features across dictionary sizes.
No large-model or open-SAE-release comparison testing size-related splitting.
The study measures spatial activation containment and intensity differences, not decoder-direction proximity or whether feature families mirror a hierarchy of concepts in the model.
The study examines one parent–child pair for absorption-like behavior; it does not vary SAE size or sparsity to test whether those changes fix absorption.
No test of larger latents decomposing into combinations of smaller latents or of larger SAEs adding novel latents.
No test that splitting is an artifact of the SAE objective or that Matryoshka objectives change or reduce splitting.

rows.subject: GraphCast
rows.stage_stated: Trained on ERA5 data from 1979 to 2017
rows.operation_detail: Measured spatial containment of Matryoshka SAE child concept 3153 within concept 99
rows.measure: Spatial containment: fraction of child firing node–timesteps where the parent also fires
rows.note: The authors describe the child as nested in the parent and report that the parent is present at 95% of the child’s firing sites.
rows.check: For V3 it is observed: the child is nested in its parent. For V4 the absorption effect is absent, because the parent fires at 95.3% of the child's sites. The record's single state 'observed' therefore misstates V4. A single state cannot express both, so read it as V3 observed and V4 absent.

source_check.correct: V3: observed (child 3153 nested in parent 99, c=0.953, 95% CI [0.949, 0.956], n=15,203). V4: absent. The parent fires at about 95% of the child's sites, and the authors say 3153 'does not take over for CONCEPT 99'.
source_check.problem: The single state 'observed' is wrong for the V4 link, where absorption is absent.

rows.subject: GraphCast
rows.stage_stated: Trained on ERA5 data from 1979 to 2017
rows.operation_detail: Compared concept 99’s containment of concept 3153 with the next-most-contained latent
rows.note: The authors say no other latent in G0 or G1 contains concept 3153, making concept 99 its unambiguous single parent.
rows.check: This is an exclusivity check (single parent), not a separate effect. Linking it to V3 is fine.

source_check.problem: Fields are right, but the verdict fix's 'exclusivity check' reading is wrong. 0.735 is another latent's containment in 99, not 3153's in a second parent: its CI width implies about 37k firings, not 3153's 15,203. Single parenthood is stated separately, with no number.

rows.stage_stated: Trained on ERA5 data from 1979 to 2017
rows.operation_detail: Compared IVT at firing sites of child concept 3153 and parent concept 99
rows.note: The child’s firing sites have higher mean IVT; the authors characterize the child as firing more on the strong end of the parent’s condition.
rows.check: It measures the IVT intensity of firing sites, not whether the parent stops firing, so it does not bear on V4. Remove V4.

rows.operation_detail: Compared the child and parent firing-site IVT distributions
rows.measure: Probability that IVT at a child firing site exceeds IVT at a parent firing site
rows.note: The text reports this probability as evidence of higher IVT at child firing sites.
rows.check: This is a distribution comparison and cannot show absorption. Remove V4.

rows.subject: GraphCast
rows.stage_stated: Trained on ERA5 data from 1979 to 2017
rows.operation_detail: Compared the fraction of child and parent firings above an IVT threshold
rows.measure: Fraction of firing sites above the threshold
rows.note: Despite the child’s greater frequency in the high-IVT tail, the authors state that it does not take over for the parent.
rows.check: This is a tail-frequency comparison. Absence of absorption is shown by r1's containment, not by this row. Remove V4.

conditions.value: G0 and G1 latents paired with later-group latents

rows.note: The authors describe the sweep as its own negative control; this aggregate reflects the lack of substantial containment for the typical candidate pair.
rows.check: This is a negative-control median over essentially random pairs. It is not a measurement of the version's effect.

rows.check: This counts nested pairs, with no expected rate or concept labels. 'Partial' is unjustified: a low share among 1.8M mostly unrelated pairs says nothing about how complete the hierarchy is.

relationships.condition: Matryoshka SAE, GraphCast layer 8, concept 99 (parent) and concept 3153 (child)
relationships.reason: The child is exclusively nested in a broad AR parent (c=0.953) and fires on the higher-intensity subset, an AR to strong-AR refinement (r1–r5). Geometric closeness was not measured.
relationships.display_finding: The child feature was exclusively nested in the broad atmospheric-river parent (c = 0.953) and fired on its higher-intensity subset, refining atmospheric rivers into strong ones. Geometric closeness was not measured.

This is nesting inside one dictionary, not splitting across sizes, and the authors call it part-whole. Geometric closeness is not measured. Both of these are untested parts, not limits.

relationships.condition: Matryoshka SAE, GraphCast layer 8, single pair 99/3153
relationships.reason: No absorption here: the parent co-fires at 95% of child sites and does not cede extreme ARs (r1). This is one pair in an architecture designed against absorption.
relationships.display_finding: No absorption appeared: the parent co-fired at 95% of child sites and did not cede extreme atmospheric rivers. This is a single pair in an architecture designed against absorption.

relation.reason: Its own nesting and no-absorption results bear on V3 and V4.

tranche.reason: New setting (GraphCast, Matryoshka SAE) with a result on nesting and on absorption. It is not T5: the authors do not argue that a version is wrong. Their part-whole remark is a terminological aside.

source_check.notes: Fixed width of 4,096, and the authors call the nested pairs part-whole rather than splitting. Containment is a mesh-footprint co-firing measure, not decoder geometry. Only one pair is characterized. r2's 0.735 is another latent's containment in 99, not an exclusivity measure.

statements.correction: 0.735 [0.730, 0.739] is the containment in 99 of 99's next-most-contained latent. The CI width implies about 37k firings, not 3153's 15,203. It shows that 3153 is the latent most contained in 99. The text states single parenthood separately, with no number: no other G0/G1 latent contains 3153.
statements.problem: All numbers are right. But '(per the verdict, r2 is an exclusivity check)' misreads 0.735. The text gives it as 99's next-most-contained latent, i.e. another latent's containment in 99, not 3153's containment in a second parent.
The text calls the sweep its own negative control (median c 0.003; 90% of pairs below 0.083) but gives no expected rate for nested pairs, so 'no baseline' holds.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: High spatial containment and the child’s concentration in stronger-IVT cases support a nested parent–child relationship in this pair; see r1, r3, r4, and r5.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Sweep of candidate pairs across Matryoshka prefix groups
reader_labels.reason: Strongly nested pairs are rare in the sweep, and the study measures spatial activation containment rather than decoder-direction proximity; see r6, r7, and r8.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The parent is present at 95% of the child’s firing sites and the authors explicitly report that the child does not take over for the parent; see r1 and r5.
